# DOC002: broken-markdown-link

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| family | DOC |
| product | frob |
| severity (default) | error |
| tier | universal |
| scope | file |
| fix | manual |
| polarity | P+ |
| must_measure | false |
| version | 1 |
| since | 2.0.0 |

A markdown link points at a missing path or a missing heading.

Relative `[text](path)` and `[text](path#anchor)` links must name an
existing file or directory (relative to the file, or to the repo root with
a leading `/`), and an anchor on a markdown target must match a heading
slug. External `http(s)` and `mailto` links, and links inside code, are
ignored. Fix the path or the anchor.

## Examples

### DOC002 broken markdown links / Fires on a missing file #1 (line 6) (fire)

```markdown
# Title

See [gone](missing.md). <!-- error: DOC002 -->
```

### DOC002 broken markdown links / Fires on a missing heading in another file #2 (line 14) (fire)

```markdown
# Title

See [it](exists.md#no-such-heading). <!-- error: DOC002 -->
```

### DOC002 broken markdown links / Fires on a missing heading in the same file #3 (line 22) (fire)

```markdown
# Title

Jump [up](#nowhere). <!-- error: DOC002 -->
```

```

### DOC002 broken markdown links / Clean for existing files and headings #6 (line 46) (clean)

See [it](exists.md), [that](exists.md#present-heading), [me](#title),
[itself](case.md#title) and [a dir](.).
```
